smell_validity.evidence: Reshaped copies of the commit pipeline sit in three entry points beside the untouched original, and the removal flow is duplicated between keyboard and row paths. Because the healthy decomposition survives as dead code, the lost single ownership of gate rules and focus announcements is unmistakable, and its drift cost on this library's core contract is compelling.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Gate changes (limit, duplicate suppression, editing covariance) now require synchronized edits in three copies, and removal focus plus screen-reader wording in two, so ordinary additions and accessibility fixes become drift-prone; the retired originals also mislead readers about live behavior. A lasting trap, though the restored boundary is subsystem-level, not architecture-level.

development_plausibility.evidence: Copies preserve behavior exactly, reshape control flow into guard branches and loop continues, and use natural state names, terminology and style consistent with the file. The endpoint-of-creep saturation of every entry point and the comments that advertise the duplication keep it just short of indistinguishable ordinary evolution.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt resolves scope, finished state and preservation boundaries: exact gate, callback, warning, announcement and focus requirements, explicit exclusions (drag-drop, portal wrapper, memo internals, public API), and repeat-everywhere plus dead-declaration clauses that rule out partial cleanup or wrong direction, while tests serve as behavioral reference and decomposition stays open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Purposes need different decisions: commit re-ownership with candidate guards, paste per-entry limit and continue ordering, removal parameterization honoring the three-way focus rule, extracting edit-input focus/change/blur semantics, re-extracting suggestion rows with escaping and renderer dispatch, and caller-audited disposal of retained declarations.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names almost every site, but classifying them requires combining the component with the utils module to find which export lost callers, and auditing retained declarations across flows, e.g. the reset helper still serves the autofocus effect. Genuinely shared utilities and memo internals must be excluded.

repair_coordination.evidence: Re-homing the commit rules determines which retained declarations and the utils export regain callers versus get removed, and restoring per-entry paste delegation fixes reset and limit ordering inside one event. Only partial repair leaves three divergent gate owners and two announcement implementations.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: The intact originals make one uniform rule dominant: re-delegate each inlined copy to its unchanged helper (commit, removal, click-through, input focus/change/blur, limit, reset, separator translation). That covers all entry-point sites, well over 80%; only the consumed Suggestions markup helpers need fresh extraction.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Specific wrong edits pass ordinary calls but fail in special states: misordered removal focus branches break deleting the first or sole tag's announcement; applying the limit gate during editing blocks updates; hoisting blur-time input clearing outside the handleInputBlur guard changes behavior. No test or execution evidence, so level 4 is unsupported.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
